1.why: The interface in all screenshots is static and uncluttered, with no moving images, animations, or pop-ups.

2.why: Primary blue buttons, bold headings, and the highlighted Stay-safe box make important actions and information stand out clearly.

3.why: Each step centers a single focused form so the main task is easy to locate, though the persistent Logs panel adds some visual noise.

4.why: The user must follow many sequential steps and remember password complexity rules (12+ chars, upper, lower, number, symbol).

5.why: No password-manager, autofill, or “remember me” options appear on any screen.

6.why: Apart from one pre-filled email, the UI offers no saved or familiar items for easy recognition.

7.why: Labels and most instructions are short and readable; only a few explanatory sentences are moderately long.

8.why: No error messages are shown in any of the eight screenshots, so the claim cannot be supported.

9.why: Password rules are stated without an example value, and most fields lack placeholders showing what to type.

10.why: The flow provides no clear choice among password, code, or face login; only a single password-plus-token/MFA path is offered.

11.why: Most steps present a single primary action; the first screen has only two or three related buttons, which is not excessive.

12.why: Green success banners and the final “Conditions accepted” message explicitly state the outcome of each major action.

13.why: Short instructional text, password-requirement tips, and the Stay-safe box supply brief help on several steps.

14.why: A Back button exists on the token step and a return button at the end, but other steps lack clear retry or correction paths.

15.why: Every screen reuses the same header, card layout, button styles, and Logs panel, keeping the design consistent.
